name: ALLAHRA DIONADJI GILCHRIST
summary: Control & Intelligent Systems Engineer with a B.Eng. in Computer Engineering and hands-on experience in PLC programming, DCS monitoring, and industrial instrumentation and control.
aboutDescription: I am Allahra Dionadji Gilchrist, a Control and Intelligent Systems Engineer with a B.Eng. in Computer Engineering from Ahmadu Bello University (ABU). My expertise bridges industrial automation, network infrastructure, and artificial intelligence to design and optimize smart, reliable systems. In the realm of control and automation, my practical experience encompasses PLC programming (Studio 5000 / RSLogix 5000), DCS supervision (Honeywell Experion PKS), PID tuning, and field instrumentation. To support these systems, I possess strong networking capabilities, specializing in industrial communication protocols such as EtherNet/IP, Modbus RTU/TCP, DeviceNet, and RS-485. Furthermore, I integrate modern AI-driven approaches into intelligent systems, utilizing computer vision (OpenCV, YOLO), digital image processing, and sensor feedback logic to develop autonomous solutions and robotics.
aboutClosing: I enjoy solving real-world engineering problems by combining reliable control systems, industrial networking, and modern AI-driven approaches such as computer vision and sensor feedback integration.

project1Abstract: This project explores an assistive wheelchair concept that combines obstacle detection with sensor feedback. A path-planning layer uses the collected data to select safer routes and support independent mobility.
project2Abstract: The irrigation prototype monitors soil moisture and automatically controls a water pump when readings fall below a configured threshold. Proteus is used to model the circuit and evaluate the control behavior before deployment.
project3Abstract: This control system maintains a target water level by measuring the tank level and adjusting the inlet flow. PID tuning is used to reduce steady-state error and keep the response stable as demand changes.
project4Abstract: This toolkit provides reusable components for inspecting industrial messages and validating protocol data. Its modular design makes it easier to test communication flows and build reliable integrations between devices.
project5Abstract: A simulated mobile robot uses ROS 2 nodes to combine localization, route planning, and obstacle avoidance. Gazebo provides a repeatable environment for testing navigation behavior before transferring the approach to physical hardware.
project6Abstract: The robot reads a marked track with onboard sensors and adjusts its motors to stay centered along the route. Obstacle detection adds a safety response that pauses motion when the path is blocked.
project7Abstract: A camera captures items moving through a sorting area, and an image-processing pipeline identifies their colors. The resulting classification is used to guide the robot toward the correct sorting position.
project8Abstract: The model analyzes equipment sensor readings to learn normal operating patterns and flag deviations for review. The goal is to help maintenance teams identify potential faults earlier and prioritize inspections.
project9Abstract: This computer-vision workflow processes production-line images to locate and classify selected components. Detection results can support visual inspection by making item presence and position easier to verify.
project10Abstract: Historical consumption data is prepared and used to train a time-series forecasting model. Short-term predictions can help operators anticipate demand and make more informed energy-management decisions.
project11Abstract: The portfolio presents engineering experience and project work through a responsive interface. Localized content and reusable project components make the site easier to browse across devices and languages.
project12Abstract: Equipment readings are delivered to a live dashboard, where operators can review current status and key operating metrics. The interface is designed to make changes and potential issues visible at a glance.
project13Abstract: The dashboard brings asset records, maintenance schedules, and work orders into one workflow. It helps organize upcoming service tasks and gives teams a clearer view of equipment maintenance history.
project14Abstract: The API provides a structured interface for collecting and serving data from industrial devices. Validation and typed responses help downstream applications consume device information consistently.
project15Abstract: The scheduler coordinates recurring work on a microcontroller with limited memory and processing capacity. Its lightweight task model helps keep periodic operations predictable without requiring a full operating system.
project16Abstract: The service accepts background jobs and distributes processing across containerized workers. Retry handling and job-status tracking make failures easier to recover from and work progress easier to monitor.
